description: We are a student team passionate about software, data, and solving real-world challenges. For NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are building FieldShift, a decision-support tool that combines NASA Earth observations.
summary:
SoilSync by Arekta Team is the NASA satellite-powered agricultural decision-support tool designed to help smallholder farmers and agricultural officers in Bangladesh's drought-prone Barind Tract make water-efficient crop decisions.
With groundwater levels declining by 10–15 metres over the past decade and Boro rice consuming 91% of irrigation water, farming is becoming unsustainable. SoilSync helps farmers identify when dry-season Boro cultivation may become economically unviable and discover better alternatives.

The platform combines NASA Earth observation data from POWER, GPM, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, and Landsat with SRDI soil data, BARI/BRRI crop characteristics, and farmers' priorities. It analyzes rainfall, soil moisture, groundwater conditions, and vegetation health to recommend suitable crop rotations based on profitability, water savings, and soil health.

For example, a one-acre demonstration in Tanore compares Boro rice with Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) against a mustard–mungbean rotation. The alternative can reduce irrigation from 28 to just 2 waterings, save approximately 75% of pumped water, and increase savings by Tk 14,300 per acre while improving soil fertility through nitrogen fixation.
Every recommendation includes transparent, traceable satellite-data evidence.
Our mission: Turn satellite intelligence into practical farming decisions that conserve groundwater, improve soil health, reduce costs, and build climate-resilient agriculture throughout Bangladesh.
details:
SoilSync by Arekta Team is a decision-support tool that tells Barind smallholders when dry-season Boro rice will lose money — and shows water-smart rotations with proof.

In the Barind Tract, groundwater has fallen 10–15m in a decade, 16,000 deep tubewells are capped at 980 pump-hours shared one year in three, yet Boro uses 91% of irrigation water (~1,605 L/kg). Farmers have no trusted way to test alternatives.

CropWise fuses NASA Earth observations (POWER heat/rain, GPM rainfall deficit, SMAP soil moisture, ECOSTRESS + Landsat stress/greenness) with SRDI soil data, BARI/BRRI crop traits, and farmer priorities (save water/soil/cost sliders). Demo — 1 acre, Tanore: keep Boro with AWD (~20% saved) vs shift to mustard + mungbean (2 waterings vs 28, ~75% pumped water + Tk14,300 saved per acre, plus nitrogen fixation). Every recommendation shows its NASA data trace in plain language. Expert HUD provides clear visualizations of datas as an expert tries to understand the farm.
